findings.title: Outdated TLS Protocol in Use
findings.ai_analysis: An outdated TLS version is in use. TLS 1.0 and 1.1 are deprecated and have known vulnerabilities including BEAST and POODLE attacks. Using these old protocols means connections may be downgraded to an insecure state by attackers.
findings.fix: Disable TLS 1.0 and 1.1. Configure server to support TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 only.

findings.title: Missing Security Header: Strict-Transport-Security
findings.description: Forces browsers to use HTTPS, preventing protocol downgrade attacks.
findings.ai_analysis: HSTS is not configured on this domain. Without HSTS, browsers may attempt HTTP connections before being redirected to HTTPS, opening a window for SSL-stripping attacks where an attacker on the same network can intercept traffic in plaintext. This is especially dangerous on public Wi-Fi.

findings.title: Missing Security Header: Content-Security-Policy
findings.description: Prevents XSS and data injection attacks by defining approved content sources.
findings.ai_analysis: No Content Security Policy (CSP) header is present. CSP is the primary defense against Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks, one of the most common and dangerous web vulnerabilities. Without a CSP, an attacker who injects malicious scripts into the page has no browser-enforced restrictions on what they can do.
findings.fix: Implement a CSP policy. Start with: Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'

findings.title: Missing Security Header: X-Frame-Options
findings.description: Prevents clickjacking by controlling if the page can be embedded in iframes.
findings.ai_analysis: The X-Frame-Options header is absent. This means your site can be embedded in an iframe on a malicious website, a technique used in clickjacking attacks. An attacker could overlay invisible UI elements on top of your site to trick users into performing unintended actions (like clicking hidden buttons or submitting forms).

findings.title: Missing Security Header: X-Content-Type-Options
findings.ai_analysis: The X-Content-Type-Options header is missing. Without it, browsers may 'sniff' the content type of a response and treat a file differently than intended, for example, loading a text file as JavaScript. This can enable MIME-type confusion attacks.

findings.title: HTTP Not Redirected to HTTPS
findings.description: Visiting the HTTP version of the site does not automatically redirect to HTTPS.
findings.evidence: http://example.com did not respond with a redirect to https://
findings.ai_analysis: HTTP traffic is not being automatically redirected to HTTPS. Users who visit the HTTP version of your site (which many do by default) will not benefit from encryption. Search engines also prefer HTTPS, so this may affect SEO.
findings.fix: Configure a 301 redirect from http:// to https:// in your web server (Nginx/Apache) or hosting platform.

findings.title: Missing Security Header: Referrer-Policy
findings.description: Controls how much referrer information is sent with requests.

findings.title: Missing Security Header: Permissions-Policy
findings.description: Controls browser features and APIs available to the page.
findings.fix: Add header: Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()

ai_summary: example.com has a moderate security posture (score: 77/100) with several areas requiring attention. 3 high-severity issues were identified that significantly increase attack surface. 6 critical HTTP security headers are missing, leaving the web application vulnerable to common browser-based attacks.
